cards.text: In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, a new king takes the throne in Judah: Hezekiah son of Ahaz. He's twenty-five years old, and his mother is Abi, the daughter of Zechariah. Pull up a stool, friend, because every king in this book gets a performance review, and this one's worth reading.

cards.question: Every king needs a home base. Where does Hezekiah, the new king of Judah, reign?

cards.text: He'll reign there twenty-nine years. TWENTY-NINE! I can't leave a batch alone for nine minutes without opening the oven door to check on it.

cards.question: True or false: King Hezekiah does what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: Just like his father David had done. And Hezekiah gets right to work: he removes the high places, shatters the sacred pillars, and then turns to the Asherah poles.

cards.question: King Hezekiah has torn out the high places and the sacred pillars. What does he do to the Asherah poles?

cards.text: Then there's a bronze snake called Nehushtan, the one Moses made back in the wilderness (Numbers 21:9). I know a thing or two about being old and kept around, friend, but this snake makes the expired coupon I shared a drawer with look BRAND new.

cards.question: What does King Hezekiah do with Nehushtan, the bronze snake Moses made?

answers.text: He puts it in the temple

cards.question: Hezekiah demolishes the bronze snake Moses made. Why?

answers.text: People had been burning incense to it
It had cracked beyond any repair
The king of Assyria wanted it

cards.text: Here's the heart of it: "Hezekiah trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel." And the writer says something about him that would make every other king in the family group chat go real quiet.

cards.question: True or false: No king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before him or after him.
Hezekiah stays faithful and doesn't turn from following the LORD. He keeps the commandments the LORD had given ___.

cards.text: "And the LORD was with Hezekiah, and he prospered wherever he went." Then he makes a BOLD move when it comes to the king of Assyria.

cards.question: Hezekiah rebels against the king of Assyria. What does he refuse to do?
Hezekiah is on a ROLL. Which people does he defeat as far as Gaza, from watchtower to fortified city?

cards.text: Meanwhile, over in Israel. In Hezekiah's fourth year, which is Hoshea's seventh, Shalmaneser king of Assyria marches against Samaria and besieges it.

cards.question: Samaria is under siege by the Assyrians. How long until they capture it?
Samaria has fallen. Where does the king of Assyria send the Israelites?
Why does all this happen to the Israelites?

answers.text: They would not listen to the LORD or obey
Their city walls were built too low
Their king trusted the wrong allies

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Keep that oven warm, because this king's story is only getting started.

findings.problem: The closing line 'every king in this book gets a performance review, and this one's worth reading' signals that Hezekiah's review is good. That rules out False on card 4, which asks whether Hezekiah did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't share the fact's core action. A 29-year reign is about lasting a long time. Not being able to leave a batch alone for nine minutes is about impatience and checking on something. The two don't click as the same action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question says Hezekiah 'has torn out the high places and the sacred pillars.' The text says he removed the high places and shattered the sacred pillars (2 Kings 18:4). Card 5 already used the text's own words.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'Something about him that would make every other king in the family group chat go real quiet' makes it plain that the writer ranks Hezekiah above the other kings. That rules out False on card 11, 'No king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before him or after him.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Their king trusted the wrong allies' can be argued as right. Hoshea, Israel's king, sent to So king of Egypt, and that led to the Assyrian siege (2 Kings 17:4). Verse 12 also frames the fall as a failure to trust and obey the LORD, so this answer is close to the right one.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 20 contains only the story-isn't-over line and retells nothing from the passage. It still cites 2 Kings 18:12, which is wider than what the card uses. However, the output format requires a verses value on every card.
findings.question: What should a final story card cite when it contains only the story-isn't-over line? Should it cite the last verse of the passage, or should verses be empty or null?
